title: Quick check: Agent Reliability and Observability

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes tracing agent decisions and actions in the context of agent reliability and observability?
options: Use the largest available model for every task and skip a baseline or documented acceptance criteria.

Tracing agent decisions and actions describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.
A fluent result is enough to establish correctness, so the input and assumptions do not need checking.
The concept can be implemented entirely in a prompt; application validation and testing are unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Tracing agent decisions and actions describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.
questions.explanation: Tracing agent decisions and actions describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next. This is why the lesson treats the concept as something to apply and verify, not as a guarantee of quality.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives the clearest evidence that monitoring tool calls and failure rates is working in agent reliability and observability?
options: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
Test only one easy input, then assume the behavior generalizes to every language, user, and data source.
Skip validation because a well-formatted answer implies the model followed the intended process.
Change the prompt, model, data, and settings at the same time, then attribute any difference to one cause.
questions.answer_key: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Monitoring tool calls and failure rates should be evaluated with evidence appropriate to its use. Representative tests and a baseline help reveal failures and avoid overstating what the example proves.

questions.prompt: A team applies tracing agent decisions and actions from agent reliability and observability and gets a plausible result, but it has not checked an edge case. What should it do next?
options: Accept the result because confidence and fluency are reliable substitutes for measurement.
Remove guardrails or access checks to make the next run more likely to succeed.
Increase model size and deploy immediately, without retaining a baseline or regression tests.
Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.explanation: A plausible answer is not proof. Controlled tests, evidence checks, and explicit uncertainty help identify incorrect assumptions and unsafe failure modes.
